items.statement: FY26 revenue expected at INR 400 crore plus with 16-16.5% EBITDA margin
items.quote: This year more or less consolidated we are going to touch INR 400 Crore or little bit plus.

items.statement: FY27 minimum 25% revenue growth targeted, EBITDA margin around 18%
items.quote: We are looking minimum 25% growth next year.

items.statement: UAE adding tempering line in Q1 FY27 to expand capacity beyond 90% IG utilization
items.quote: We are adding capacity in the form of tempering line, so that is going to commence in the first quarter of the next year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target 18% for FY27, up from 16-16.5% in FY26
items.quote: So we are targeting EBITDA of around 18%.

items.statement: Fire-rated and bulletproof glass expected to deliver higher margins than current products
items.quote: The new product like fire-rated and the bulletproof will definitely give a higher margin.

items.statement: Strong demand from residential, commercial, data centers, infrastructure, and hospitality sectors
items.quote: Particularly in the metro cities demand on the luxury segment, you know, is increasing, like high-rise buildings, bigger flats, and so on.

items.statement: Railway/Vande Bharat orders approved and supplying, contribution to grow gradually
items.quote: Our products are been approved and we had already started supply but eventually as of now the contribution is very less but definitely in the coming quarters it will be more.

items.statement: Glasstech Taloja and Erode units acquired in June-July, under consolidation, expected to contribute INR 150 cr revenue at 15% EBITDA at optimum utilization
items.quote: We have a potential to generate more than INR150 crores of revenue and EBITDA will be around in the range of 15%.

items.statement: Raised INR 72.15 cr via preferential equity at INR 555/share and INR 5.5 cr via 25% warrant upfront payment
items.quote: The company has allotted 13 lakh equity share of face value of INR10 each by way of preferential issue at an issue price of INR555 per share, including share premium of INR545 per share, aggregating INR72.15 crores.

items.statement: Promoter loans of INR 28 cr repaid in Q3 FY26, debt-equity now below 0.5x
items.quote: In the December quarter we had already repaid some of the promoter loans of around INR28 crores from the fund what we had raised from an equity and the warrants issue.

items.statement: Sole supply agreement with Saint-Gobain for 55% of raw material (glass) ensures stable pricing and supply
items.quote: For the major raw material, which is a 55% of our raw material, is glass, and for that we have a now sole supply agreement with the Saint-Gobain.

items.statement: India-UAE revenue mix expected to reach 50-50 or 55-45 in next two years from current UAE-heavy mix
items.quote: Going forward in next two years, mostly, it will be equal. Both the side, India will be the same and UAE will be also same or there will be 55-45 or the reverse 45-55 on turnover.

items.statement: Potential acquisition under due diligence, legal process ongoing, decision expected in a month
items.quote: We have one plant, where the due diligence is over and certain legal process is on. So on certain valuations point and certain legal point, the deal is under process.

items.statement: No plans to raise equity capital currently; no need seen.
items.quote: Are there plans to raise equity capital? Not right now. We don't see a need for it.

items.statement: Insurance business expanded to Kolkata and Raipur; aim to operate in all markets with significant physical presence phase-wise.
items.quote: We have expanded to Kolkata and we will be slowly expanding to Raipur as well. Over time, we want to operate our insurance plan in all the markets where we have a significant physical presence. But we will be opening it up phase wise.

items.statement: FY26 revenue expected at INR560-570 crores, stable vs prior year INR550 crores
items.quote: FY '26 is more or less actually stable only, say, we have touched INR400 crores now and INR170 crores, INR160 crores maybe another March end. So say, it will be last year it was INR550 crores, so maybe INR560 crores, INR570 crores.

items.statement: Incurred ~INR65 crores capex in FY26 YTD; benefits expected from FY27
items.quote: The company continued to expand its business, made ~65 crores capex till date in this FY, we believe next financial year will be very good for the Company as we will start getting benefit of the capex done by the company in this financial year in next financial year.

items.statement: Holds order book of ~500 cold chain vehicles; AC vehicle cost INR65-70 lakhs each
items.quote: Now, we have a total order of around 500 cars in our hands. Because this is a huge investment and high capex business. So, an AC car is made which is around INR65 lakhs-INR70 lakhs.

items.statement: Warehousing expansion target: 9 lakh sq ft currently to 15 lakh sq ft by FY27 (5 lakh sq ft addition in Guwahati, Patna)
items.quote: As of now, we are managing around 9 lakh square feet. And our target for next year is around 15 lakh square feet. 5 lakh square feet is coming up in Guwahati and Patna.

items.statement: Missed prior revenue targets (INR700 cr FY26, INR1000 cr FY27-28) due to lost contracts; taking corrective action
items.quote: We missed one or two contract, but we will take corrective action and it will be fine. We are doing very hard.

items.statement: Long-term FMCG supply chain contract won with zero capex and decent margins
items.quote: We entered into long term contract with renowned FMCG company for supply chain management services without any capex with decent margin.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of INR 370-380 crore for FY27 confirmed as conservative; expects results to be much better
items.quote: those number are intact, and that was the actual, very much conservative number. So we are believing that, result would be much better than what, 370 to 380 Crores.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target INR 190-200 crore (Anlon INR 160-170 cr + Apiqo INR 20-25 cr)
items.quote: INR 160 Cr to 170 Cr from Anlon, and Apico is almost, considering our, this month's revenue and next month's order book, INR 20-25 Cr from ApiQo. So consolidated, it would be somewhere around INR 190 to 200 Cr.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margins around 60% for FY27-28
items.quote: It would be somewhere around 60%.

items.statement: Kharsang targeting 1,000+ bpd oil production with existing wells
items.quote: The production plan per se is about targeting about 1,000-plus barrels with the existing well.

items.statement: Plans 18 shallow and 3 deep wells in Kharsang, 4 in Dirok, 2 in Greater Dirok, 2 each in Asjol and Palej onshore; 10 offshore wells (3 PY-1, 3 B-80, 4 B-15)
items.quote: We remain committed to drilling a total of 18 shallow wells and 3 deep wells in Kharsang, 4 wells in Dirok, 2 wells in Greater Dirok and 2 wells each in Asjol and Palej in our onshore assets. To unlock the potential of our offshore fields, we plan to drill 10 offshore wells, 3 wells in PY-1, 3 wells in B-80 and 4 wells

items.statement: DNPL-IGGL pipeline hook-up expected by end March 2026; gas offtake increase expected by Q1 FY27
items.quote: We expect it should get completed by March 2026 and the augmentation of the offtakes should take place at least by the first quarter of the next year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA Rs 31 crore in Q3 FY26 vs Rs 25 crore in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the current quarter is Rs. 31 crores in the consol accounts compared to Rs. 25 crores in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Both debt and equity options open for funding if HPCL dues not resolved; board to decide
items.quote: It is up to the board to have a look at it, and both options are open at the moment.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 55 crore, cash Rs 30 crore as of call date
items.value: Rs 55 crore debt, Rs 30 crore cash
items.quote: Rs. 55 crore debt and the cash is about Rs. 30 crores cash is there.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 manufacturing turnover expected to be better than Q3 FY26
items.quote: But yes Q4 will be better than Q3 in terms of the manufacturing turnover.

items.statement: PP yarn JV (ESSEKAN) expected to generate INR20-25 crore revenue in FY27
items.quote: This year, we expect a revenue of about INR20 crores to INR25 crores in this year -- in the next financial year, sorry.

items.statement: Total capex plan of INR99 crore includes FIBC expansion (INR20 crore), roll management system, and non-woven project (INR55 crore)
items.quote: Yes, so there is a INR99 crores capex that we announced last quarter. It has multiple sections. So the it has a phased capex program which includes 6,000 tons of FIBC capacity expansion over the next 5 years in a new building in unit 3 itself.

items.statement: FIBC capacity expansion of 6,000 tons over 5 years at Unit 3, building 30% complete, targeting May 2026 completion
items.quote: The construction of the building of FIBC expansion at Unit 3 is approximately 30% completed, target for completion in May '26. This will add an incremental target of up to 6,000 tons per annum in the next five years

items.statement: Order book remains stable and comfortable; domestic demand boosted by jute packaging act dilution allowing PP woven sacks for food grains
items.quote: So the order book remains extremely stable. Nothing to be worried about. Neither it is too long nor it is too short. It is absolutely where we are comfortable.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin 9.1% in Q3 FY26; manufacturing EBITDA 10.5%; FIBC margin 12.5-13.5%, fabric and multifilament ~7% each
items.quote: So as you must have seen, the blen ded EBITDA is about 9%. The manufacturing EBITDA is at about 10.5%. Within that 10.5%, if you break it down into all the four product segments that we are into which is FIBC, PP woven fabric, commodity multifilament yarn and UV masterbatch, the EBITDA margins of fabric is about at 7%,

items.statement: Export EBITDA margin 11.5-12%, domestic EBITDA margin ~6.5%
items.quote: So the blended obviously we know. The exports EBITDA is around 11.5% to 12% and domestic is at about 6.5%.

items.statement: FIBC share of manufacturing turnover to rise from 54% to 70-75% over next few years; fabric to decline from 28% to ~10%
items.quote: So FIBC is 54%, fabric is 28%, multifilament is 10% and others are 8%. So MFI and -- Yes, I am answering that. So MFI and others will remain at 10% and 8%. This fabric 28% will become about 10% and this 54% will become about 70% to 75%.

items.statement: Polymer costs up 10-15% due to crude oil increase but fully passed on to customers; no inflation risk
items.quote: On the raw material side yes you are right, like all other commodities and crude oil has also gone up, polymer has also gone up by about 10% to 15%. But as you know in our industry this gets passed on to the customer. So there is no inflation risk from that standpoint.

items.statement: US tariff clarity (18%) and EU FTA (0% duty from next year) positive for medium-term demand; Europe remains largest market at 62% of exports
items.quote: The EU FTA is also an extremely important point that has come in because from a long term sustainability of the business in India with a 0% tariff into EU, India will remain the most competitive across other emerging manufacturing countries.

items.statement: Valex Ventures (UK) acquisition is strategic platform; no significant revenue or profit contribution expected for couple of years
items.quote: It will take a couple of years to see any significant results, because the end user marketing and B2C relationship takes time to break in.

items.statement: Non-woven needle punch project (INR55 crore) for automotive, geotextiles, artificial leather, footwear; phased, demand-led scaling
items.quote: The third portion of it is the technical textiles non-woven needle punch. That would go into the automotive segment, artificial leather, footwear, geotextiles and filtration fabrics. So that is at about INR55 crores.

items.statement: Steady-state gross margin expected at 44-45% average per quarter going forward
items.quote: If we say that what this could look like as a trend in the coming quarters also, we could say that this would somewhere look like somewhere between 44% to 45%, on an average for a quarter.

items.statement: Secured credit distribution scaling expected in H2 FY27 after building open API stack and supply side
items.quote: I think H2 next year is where we can hopefully see that numbers scale.

items.statement: New engine investments reduced from Rs 11 crore last FY to ~Rs 1 crore per quarter currently
items.quote: almost Rs. 11 crores we have done in the last financial year on these new engines, which has now come down to kind of Rs. 1 crore a quarter.

items.statement: AePS market share reached 18.64% in Off-Us segment in Q3 FY26
items.quote: We have closed Quarter 3 at close to 18.64% market share in the Off-Us segment and we continue to consolidate our market share in this segment.

items.statement: Nine-month PAT rose to Rs 21 crore from Rs 4 crore YoY driven by gross margin growth and flat indirect costs
items.quote: If you see on the YTD numbers, the PAT is almost Rs. 21 crores against Rs. 4 crores in the previous year, nine months.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to ~47% in Q3 aided by direct cost optimization and favorable CMS client mix shift
items.quote: We have been optimizing on that. And that has led to this improvement in our gross margins.

items.statement: UPI Cash Point launch targeted for end of Q4 FY26 to enable cash withdrawal via UPI at agent network
items.quote: Towards the close of this Quarter 4, we are looking to enable customers to be able to withdraw cash using UPI.

items.statement: Credit disbursements hit Rs 19.2 crore in Q3 FY26 vs Rs 20.5 crore full FY25; Vyapar loans launched with Muthoot Fincorp
items.quote: In this quarter alone, we have delivered disbursements of almost Rs. 19.2 crore.

items.statement: Insurance launched in Q2; ~10,000 policies sold to date; FD-backed credit cards with ZET at ~2,500 cards sold
items.quote: We launched this product in Q2 on a couple of categories. And till date, we have sold almost 10,000 policies so far.

items.statement: Labor code impact booked as exceptional item; deferred tax asset created on gratuity/leave provisions
items.quote: There is also one point with respect to the labor code impact, which has come as an exceptional item, which we have shown as a net of tax purposes.

items.statement: Collections business under pressure due to MFI/NBFC book consolidation; may persist 1-2 quarters
items.quote: We are seeing some short term pressures and maybe they will continue for a quarter or two until we are able to look at enhancing our product suite around digital collections.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance maintained at INR500-550 crores, dependent on MoD inspection completion by March 31
items.quote: Yes. Now the year is coming to closer to end, and we have stocks, which need to be inspected and delivered to MoD. So if the inspections are completed and then delivery is completed, yes. If it gets into, then it will go to the next quarter.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance conservatively estimated at INR500-600 crores based on current year experience
items.quote: We are expecting INR500 crores to INR600 crores turnover next year.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR60 crores for Katepally and PDK plant expansions including RDX/HMX, propellant manufacturing and rocket motor integration
items.quote: Yes, around INR60 crores is the capex for Katepally and PDK together.

items.statement: INR429 crore MoD order for chaffs/flares received in October 2025, 50% to be executed within 1 year
items.quote: In October, we secured a major order worth INR429 crores from the Ministry of Defense, Government of India for the supply of chaffs and flares to the Indian Air Force.

items.statement: Export orders include price escalation clauses to protect against raw material cost increases
items.quote: And we -- every export order we execute or we take, we are including a price escalation clause from year-on-year so that the price increase in the raw materials is protected.

items.statement: Coal India bulk explosives not supplied due to unviable pricing; servicing Singareni Collieries instead
items.quote: Coal India, the prices are so low. So unless we get our price at a reasonable price, which at least breaks even, we are not entering into that.

items.statement: MPS targets 20-25% year-on-year earnings growth and INR 1500 crores revenue at similar margins
items.quote: Our appetite is to grow at 20 %, -25% year-on-year. So if you track MPS earnings growth from FY'21, we've been growing at a PBT CAGR of 21%. In order to get that level of growth in the market that we operate in, you have to have a blend of organic and inorganic growth. And with the vision that we have of getting to INR

items.statement: Unbound standalone EBITDA margin is 14%; MPS expects rapid expansion to early 20s in Q2 FY27 via shared services
items.quote: Incoming EBITDA margin is 14% standalone without any MPS involvement. So, the first three months we'll probably continue with the same level of EBITDA margin. That will then grow very quickly in the next quarter to the early 20% EBITDA margin. And by the exit of Q4 FY'27, we'll be closer to 30%.

items.statement: Healthcare AI knowledge management market projected to grow from $3B to $102B by 2034 at 42% CAGR; 10M health worker deficit by 2033
items.quote: Unbound is particularly focused on the AI -driven knowledge management subsector, which is expected to grow from $ 3 billion to $ 102 billion by 2034 at a staggering 42% CAGR. As hospitals in the U.S. shift from manual databases to intelligent smart agents through agentic AI , Unbound is perfectly positioned through th

items.statement: Unbound adds Nursing Central, uCentral, Society Solutions with AI-native platform; MPS to cross-sell content services to Unbound's marquee US university clients
items.quote: Now, can I go to a marquis US university, which is Unbound's largest customer , and say right now you're using the Unbound platform for enabling off-the-shelf content. Can I actually build custom courses for you? And enable the executive education and the continuing education arm of this marquis US university?

items.statement: Acquisition funded with INR 42 crores debt; final transaction value $15.18M after working capital adjustments; no earn-outs
items.quote: We've raised INR 42 crores of debt. and from my perspective, we're very comfortable with this level of debt. We have a good balance sheet. Our DSO is now closer to 45 days instead of 60 days. So assuming this level of debt , we'll be comfortable as a board to continue to distribute surplus capital through dividends and

items.statement: INR 42 crores debt raised for acquisition; comfortable with leverage given DSO improvement to 45 days
items.quote: We've raised INR 42 crores of debt. and from my perspective, we're very comfortable with this level of debt. We have a good balance sheet. Our DSO is now closer to 45 days instead of 60 days.

items.statement: No earn-outs; Unbound management retained with phantom options; Bill Detmer transitions to strategic advisor role
items.quote: No, there are no earn-outs. The transaction is complete. I know that we had provided as the disclosure requirements require us to provide a transaction value of $ 16.5 million. That said, post-closing adjustments will apply, and the final transaction value will be updated accordingly.

items.statement: MPS plans geographic expansion of Unbound into Europe, APAC, Middle East, Australia; cross-sell via existing MPS partnerships in China and other markets
items.quote: We plan to integrate global delivery, expand the product suite with Unbound Intelligence and Assist, and scale into new institutional markets in Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Europe, and Australia.

items.statement: Management expects bullish growth in coming quarters driven by solar sector CAPEX and settled US tariffs
items.quote: So, we are very bullish about the coming quarter, where a lot of activities are happening, especially when the solar companies are looking at a big CAPEX in the next two quarters, and there will be a lot of plants and machinery which they will be importing.

items.statement: Solar companies planning big CAPEX in next two quarters will drive import logistics demand
items.quote: We are very bullish about handling logistics for them. And we have already catered for the required bench strength to handle that business.

items.statement: TiGreen vertical contributes over 40% of total revenue and volumes growing continuously
items.quote: TiGreen is doing very well for us. We are very bullish. The volumes are growing continuously. It is contributing more than 40% to our total revenue.

items.statement: Volume grew 9% quarter-to-quarter and close to 50% year-on-year despite geopolitical headwinds
items.quote: We were able to do good volumes, and the volume is up by 9% quarter-to-quarter and almost close to year-on-year. If we have to look at the business volume, that is also up by close to 50% year-on-year.

items.statement: Revenue dipped due to lowest ever freight levels under cost-plus model, but volume growth indicates business penetration
items.quote: There has been a small dip in the overall top line. That is primarily because ours is a cost-plus model, and the freight in this quarter has been the lowest ever.

items.statement: Pharma sector exports from North India region showing good growth after new office opening
items.quote: We have had a good penetration in the pharma sector also, that is from the upper north region, where we had six months back, we had opened our big office in the upper north region, covering the pharma sector of Punjab, Haryana and Himachal belt.

items.statement: CUBOX LCL vertical broke even after one year but below expectations; FCL remains preferred model
items.quote: CUBOX is taking slightly longer. We have almost completed one year, but whatever the expected numbers are, maybe the expectations were more. It is not on the same lines as we were expecting it to be. But still it is, it is the overall vertical is breaking even and giving some profits.

items.statement: Hydrogen MOU with Russia on hold due to huge CAPEX requirements and immature market
items.quote: On the hydrogen, we are not doing much in that. We are going slow because that involves huge CAPEX. The market is still evolving. It is not mature at all. So, we are still evaluating the market.

items.statement: Open to inorganic acquisitions in international logistics but no suitable targets found
items.quote: We are open to any inorganic acquisition, which we have also gone through that in an inorganic way also. But unfortunately, we have not been able to get a good company.

items.statement: Air freight decline due to US tariff issues and European slowdown; considered negligible to overall business
items.quote: Air freight business decline is primarily because of the tariff issues, and the European business is going down and the tariff issues which are happening. So, people were not buying, especially the high fashion goods and garments and similar kinds of products which move primarily by air.

items.statement: Focus on deepening penetration in established verticals (solar, auto, government) before pursuing new businesses
items.quote: So, we want to focus on them and reach more respectable numbers and more numbers where we are in the top five, top three category. And then the focus is on new business. So, that is our policy, and that is what we are going to do.

items.statement: Tax implication expected to be less than 1% of turnover under tonnage tax scheme from current year
items.quote: The guidance would be anywhere between less than 1% of the turnover as the total tax implication. That is what we believe it is going to be.

items.statement: Current quarter performance considered as benchmark for future
items.quote: We have moved towards higher revenue, higher profit margin. So, this can be considered as the benchmark going forward into the future.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR1,500 crores with dredging INR409 crores, charter hire INR863 crores, shipbuilding INR230 crores
items.quote: Order book of the Company as on date stands at INR1,500 crores, out of which, dredging order book is INR409 crores, charter hire order book INR863 crores, including green tug contracts; and shipbuilding order book stands at INR230 crores.

items.statement: Bids in pipeline exceed INR3,000 crores across dredging, chartering and shipbuilding
items.quote: Bids in pipeline stands at more than INR3,000 crores; dredging orders in pipeline INR1,400 crores; chartering INR1,000 crores; and shipbuilding INR704 crores.

items.statement: INR183 crores allocated for capex from INR285 crores fund raise, to be deployed over 3 years
items.quote: We have raised fund raise of INR285 crores for which the allocation was as follows capex INR183 crores, working capital INR30 crores and under GCP i.e., General Corporate Purpose, INR71 crores

items.statement: INR100 crores investment planned for shipyard expansion to build tugs and smaller vessels
items.quote: So, we are going to invest close to INR100 crores in the shipyard, which is going to be a mix of debt and equity.

items.statement: Inland waterway dredging demand expected to increase multifold over next 5 years with 20 national waterways to be made navigable
items.quote: Because you must have seen in the budget right now, almost 20 more national waterways have been required to be made navigable, and this demand is huge. So, over the next 5 years, in the inland waterway, dredging demand is going to increase in multifold.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin at 43%, PAT margin at 34% with improved operating leverage
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR38.54 crores with a margin of 43%, reflecting a strong improvement in operating efficiency. Profit after tax stood at INR32.89 crores, with a margin of 34%.

items.statement: No direct competition with Dredging Corporation of India as they focus on larger vessels while company operates in shallow draft and river dredging
items.quote: We do not believe that DCI is direct competition right now or we are direct competition to DCI. But because the demand is so high, there is enough space for more than 2 players to be in the field.

items.statement: Bahrain project on hold until suitable vessel found at lower cost than current River Pearl 18
items.quote: We are currently actively looking for a vessel in the market to place it in Bahrain and start the business. We have not kept on hold the Bahrain Project. As soon as the vessel is identified and purchased and deployed, the business can commence.

items.statement: Shipyard facility expected to achieve INR500-700 crores top line within 3 years
items.quote: We believe that we can reach a top line of between INR500 crores to INR700 crores with the facility 3 years down the line.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin compressed to ~1.5% due to supply chain cost absorption on fixed-price contracts and loss of a hyperscale telecom client
items.quote: Q3 was a challenging quarter due to global semiconductor shortages and supply chain disruptions, which impacted hardware availability and led to pricing pressures. Despite these headwinds, we executed committed orders to maintain strong customer relationships, though this resulted in temporary margin pressure.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 order book stands at approximately Rs 200 crore covering infrastructure deployment, cloud and managed services contracts
items.quote: The current order book for Q4 is of around Rs. 200 crore which includes our infrastructure deployment projects as well as cloud and managed services contracts.

items.statement: Digital India Corporation 3-year managed services contract worth Rs 15 crore per quarter (Rs 60 crore ARR) with good margins and no hardware dependency
items.quote: Fantastic. So, Mahesh, of course, it is an annuity-based contract, Rs. 15 crores repeated every quarter this is happening, so yearly this may contribute us Rs. 60 crores of revenue. This is ARR, and this contract is there for minimum three years, extended further. So, this is annuity-based, number one, and the margin c

items.statement: Semiconductor shortage driven by AI/GPU demand expected to persist through entire FY27, keeping component prices elevated
items.quote: So, semiconductor challenge will be throughout 2027. Okay, means the entire FY'27, there will be a challenge.

items.statement: New service delivery center inaugurated in Navi Mumbai (Turbhe) for 24x7 NOC/SOC, cybersecurity, cloud and managed services; full utilization expected in 24-36 months
items.quote: Additionally, the company inaugurated a new service delivery center in Navi Mumbai, Turbhe to enhance 24x7 monitoring, cybersecurity, cloud, and managed services capabilities.

items.statement: Targeting hyperscalers, GCCs and GIFT City entrants as key growth vectors; mid-market segment remains sweet spot at 31.78% of revenue
items.quote: New hyperscalers or the people who are trying to build hyperscalers in India is one of the focuses, along with GCC, GIFT cities, people coming into the GIFT cities, and the GCC are the next focus for us to increase our business.

items.statement: Cloud/data center revenue ~Rs 250+ crore; managed services including infrastructure ~Rs 100+ crore annually
items.quote: So, you can take cloud is around Rs. 250 plus crores. Managed services, including infrastructure managed services is around Rs. 100 plus crores.

items.statement: Management expects Q4 FY26 to be very positive and bullish, targeting TEU volumes close to FY25 levels of ~112,800 TEUs
items.quote: Q4 FY26 would be very positive and company is very bullish from Q4 FY26 onwards.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin target is double-digit, up from ~9% in 9M FY26, driven by asset deployment and cost reduction
items.quote: So, the margins what we are currently in 9M FY26 I think our EBITDA is close to 9% odd. So, we are very, very positive going on a double-digit.

items.statement: Deploying ~INR 130 crore in FY26 and Q1 FY27 for trucking, trailers, and containers; 70-75 trailers in Q4 FY26, balance 60-70 in Q1 FY27; 1,000 containers in Q4 FY26
items.quote: We are deploying assets in FY26 and Q1 FY27 combined close to INR 130-odd crores especially on trucking and transport and containers.

items.statement: Signed contracts with multiple customers for energy storage battery (BESS) movements; executing auto contracts in Q4 FY26; identified sizable customers in engineering and pharma
items.quote: We already started signing contracts with multiple customers and we also started executing in different ports in India.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin compressed to 2.8% (vs 7.4% 9M) due to 28-30% freight rate drop and customer retention strategy; cost of services rose to 91% of revenue
items.quote: Due to market dynamics, the prices were the base and the freight rates were softening. We also wanted to maintain our existing customer base.

items.statement: Average revenue per TEU fell ~16% QoQ from ~INR 79,000 to ~INR 67,000; freight rates dropped 28-30%; management passed on lower rates to retain customers
items.quote: For an example in Q2 FY26 the average per TEU cost was around 79,000 and for this quarter Q3 FY26 it is close to 67,000 odd. So, there has been almost like a 16% drop in terms of the pricing.

items.statement: Renewable energy import volumes declined due to ALMM policy and US policy uncertainty; engineering products revenue share doubled to 20.2%; auto sector growth expected in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Due to this policy kind of fluctuations especially from the US, every manufacturer was very cautious about piling up their raw material which brought down the volume especially on the renewable sectors.

items.statement: Sea import 79% of revenue; sea export share rose to 14.5% from 12.2% QoQ; engineering products vertical grew to 20.2% from 10.8%; Asia 83% of revenue
items.quote: Sea export show gradual improvement in share, increasing about 14.5% of revenue as compared to 12.2% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Policy changes (ALMM, US trade policy) causing demand volatility; driver scarcity delaying fleet deployment; freight rate softness pressuring margins
items.quote: The market is very soft in Q3 FY26, due to lot of policy changes, policy angles especially from our country's policy against the Southeast Asia countries policy.

items.statement: Opened new branch in Ahmedabad; total 9 branches now; fleet increased to 42 owned vehicles with 25 added in Q3 FY26
items.quote: During the quarter, we opened new branch in Ahmedabad to strengthen our presence in West India and to support customer in that region with faster coordination and on-ground service.

items.statement: Export volumes expected to grow minimum 15% in FY27
items.quote: Exports, we are doing quite fine. And I believe that next financial year, our exports should jump by minimum 15%.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin to improve by 200-250 bps
items.quote: Even I tell you our fourth-quarter EBITDA will definitely grow by minimum 200 to 250 basis points more.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA expected to remain intact given aged inventory
items.quote: And for the next financial year, since we are holding stocks for more than 1 year, 1.5 years, for next financial year also looking at the market, our EBITDA is going to be intact.

items.statement: Saudi business progressing well with regular shipments via wholesalers; distributor not finalized
items.quote: The Saudi business is progressing well, and we are seeing consistent volume demand with regular shipment taking place.

items.statement: Domestic FY27 growth expected mid-single to early double-digit; e-commerce salience rising
items.quote: I think we are very positive that we can maintain mid-single-digit growth or maybe even early double-digit growth

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margins around 8% expected over medium term from FY27 onwards

items.quote: From FY28 onwards, Dewas can generate around INR100-plus-crores of annual revenue at optimal utilization

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 97 bps to 9.8% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margins expanded by 97 basis points to 9.8%, supported by operating leverage, improved product mix and cost optimization across operations.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals contributed 62% of chemical basket in 9M FY26
items.quote: So as we saw that the spec chem have contributed 62% of the chemical basket in 9 month FY26.

items.quote: The industry has been requesting the government for an increase in the price for ethanol from B-heavy molasses or from sugarcane juice commensurate with the increase in cane price that has happened over the last two to three years for which there is no corresponding increase in ethanol price.

items.quote: The company is advancing well in the development of its cancer molecule to find a solution to treating triple negative breast cancer which is currently the hardest to treat breast cancer variety. items.quote: Our recent MOU with Synthomer which is an MOU to show the use of our bio-based butanol for the use of their monomer butyl acrylate is one such exercise in advancing this endeavour of making specialty chemicals bio-based come forward.

items.statement: Consumer brand Jivana crossed INR100 crores revenue in 9M FY26; distribution at 7,500+ outlets; brand spend in single-digit crores
items.quote: Our brand portfolio Jivana crossed INR100 crores revenue during 9 months of FY26, validating our strategy of building a balanced business model that combines the industrial strength with consumer-facing growth.

items.statement: Exceptional provision made for new labour code implementation costs in Q3 FY26
items.quote: In this particular quarter, we've had to make an estimate for the costs that we may have to incur due to the implementation of the new labour code. And so that is why we have made an additional provision in this quarter.

items.statement: Group confident of exceeding Rs 550 crore sales this year, possibly better.
items.quote: the group is now poised to exceed about 550 crores of sales this year. We may even do better than that.

items.statement: TPMS opportunity with Bosch, Conti, Sensata could be Rs 100-150 crore annually; 5-year order book over Rs 500 crore.
items.quote: if I take a five year picture, right, I would say that the order book would be in the order of magnitude of 500 core plus, right, or a five year period.

items.statement: Expects to keep pushing EBITDA margin higher each quarter going forward.
items.quote: we do expect that going forward, we would continue to build on that and we'll be continuing to push that EBITDA margin higher and higher with each passing quarter, right.

items.statement: Sales mix shifting toward higher-EBITDA products; further improvement expected in Q4, Q1 and next FY.
items.period: Q4 FY26, Q1 FY27, next financial year
items.quote: we do believe going into Q4 and Q1 as well into the next financial year, we would be seeing further improvements on this number, right.

items.statement: Pushing customers for price corrections on non-RM costs like manpower, consumables, power not compensated for long.
items.quote: We are pushing the customers now to get those you know price corrections through for us.

items.statement: Need to allocate capital for new initiatives, metals vertical growth, and TPMS product line for global customers.
items.quote: we need to allocate funds for our new initiative and we need to ensure that, you know, we fund the growth for the metals vertical, for the TPMS product line that we are setting up now for some of our global customers.

items.statement: TPMS mass production for Aumovio and Sensata expected in next six to nine months; Bosch already in mass production.
items.quote: we will go into mass production for continently anywhere in the next I would say six to nine months, we will go into mass production for Aumovio as well.

items.statement: Tube-to-tubeless transition to complete in 4-5 years; Triton better positioned with higher margins in tubeless.
items.quote: over the next maybe four or five years that transition will happen almost completely where you know tube will almost become insignificant and tubeless will be the product that will rule the market, right.

items.statement: Metals vertical developing special alloys; orders received, expect orders to increase in Q4 and Q1.
items.quote: We've already received orders for some of these you know alloys and we expect that going into Q4 and Q1, we are, we expect that those orders will only go on increasing for us.

items.statement: Board recommended 3:1 bonus; process to complete by 11 April 2026 via securities premium account.
items.quote: we propose to issue three bonus shares of rupees ten, each fully paid up for every share that shareholders are holding.

items.statement: Metals business profitability focus starting to show in Q3; more expected in Q4 and Q1.
items.quote: So a little bit of that profitability focus has started coming through in the Q3 and we'll see more of that going into Q4 and Q1.

items.statement: New India-US and EU trade deals seen as tailwinds for exports to those markets.
items.quote: some of the new trade deals that India has made with US and EU, those will be further tailwinds for us because those are markets that are very keen to start working with us

items.statement: Climate control vertical currently loss-making; goal to keep losses minimal amid market conditions.
items.quote: The climate control business currently is loss making. So our goal in Q3 was to, you know, keep that damage under control, make sure that, you know, we, we keep that loss as small as possible

items.statement: Targeting consolidated revenue of ~Rs 600 crore in FY26, up from earlier Rs 550 crore estimate.
items.quote: Even though we've set 550 I think we would love to have that number as close to $600. As 600 this this year itself.

items.quote: I said directionally that we are aiming to cross 10 % on the EBITDA number, right. Somewhere between, yeah, somewhere around Q4 and perhaps going into Q1.

items.statement: Price corrections of 4-8% sought from long-pending OEM customers; partial flows received in Q3, more expected in Q4 and Q1.
items.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26, Q1 FY27
items.quote: We've been asking them a certain figure. It could be anywhere between 4 to 8 % in terms of the correction that they need to make on the pricing, right.

items.statement: Automotive vertical capex of Rs 5-8 crore per year for next 3 years; no significant capex for brass mill.
items.quote: In the automotive vertical, we expect that the average CapEx per year would be somewhere in the range of five to eight cores. Right. That would be the kind of CapEx that we'll be looking at each year.

items.statement: US customer order traction improving after tariff clarity; positive developments with Lenux and other US/Taiwan customers.
items.quote: I do believe that, you know, we will see a lot of traction in the US market, be it Lenux or any other customer. We do see that, you know, the order positions, the order's already going up.

items.quote: These vents are sold at anywhere between, I would say, about, about about a hundred to I would say a hundred eighty rupees per piece.

items.statement: Heavy capex phase is over; no new capex needed until capacity is utilized.
items.quote: The heavy Capex phase, which we have been investing so far, is behind us now.

items.statement: Current footprint supports 1 million vehicles and 6 GWh cell capacity; revenue potential ₹15,000-20,000 crores.

items.quote: service backlogs have reduced nearly 50% from 14 days to around 7-8 days now, and we are now completing 80% of service tickets on the same day.

items.quote: We are currently at 2.5 gigawatt hour install capacity, scaling to 6 gigawatt hour by March 2026.
